A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same Inst3D-LMM work, with corresponding sections, equations, Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–9. Neither supplied PDF includes an appendix, although both reference supplementary material. The supplied content supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Inst3D-LMM benchmark results in Tables 1–2, component ablations in Tables 3–8, and efficiency measurements in Table 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark, ablation and efficiency results in Tables 1–9. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same feature extraction, MCMF fusion, 3D-ISR spatial modeling and joint instruction-tuning procedures. No component, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanNetv2-based coverage: ScanRefer and Multi3DRefer grounding, ScanQA question answering, and Scan2Cap captioning. The qualitative scenarios in Figure 7 are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the benchmark and ablation comparisons, including Chat-Scene, Grounded 3D-LLM, LL3DA, ViL3DRel and Q-Former in their respective experiments. The two newly cited works are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain unchanged, including the 1,201/312 training/validation scene split, five selected views, three crop levels, evaluation metrics and backbone configurations. No experiment introduces a new protocol.

E4.justification: Tables 3–9 retain the same fusion, spatial-relation, CLS-token, distance/orientation, module-combination, backbone and efficiency analyses. Figures 5–7 retain the same qualitative comparisons and visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Point-score and approximate resource reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Tables 1–2 report the same ScanRefer Acc@0.50 of 51.6, ScanQA CIDEr of 88.6, and Scan2Cap CIDEr@0.50 of 79.7. Citation renumbering does not alter results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(7), including spatial-feature construction and attention formulas, are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about instance-aware fusion, spatial-relation modeling, generalist instruction tuning without task-specific fine-tuning, and improved performance and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of module effectiveness and token-related efficiency remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning scarce 3D-text data, the gap to embodied action control, and hallucination and safety concerns.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same frozen feature extractors, LoRA tuning, AdamW optimizer with 0.02 weight decay, eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs and code link. No implementation or access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds v2 references [46], 'Moiré backdoor attack (MBA)', and [47], 'Physical adversarial attack meets computer vision: A decade survey', to the existing sentence about semantic pixels lost during sparse fusion. Other works are retained and renumbered; the broader positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 corrects one occurrence of 'close-set' to 'closed-set'. Apart from citation updates and associated line wrapping, the prose, section order and explanations remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citations cause limited paragraph reflow and bibliography reflow across pages 10–11. Figure artwork, table structures, captions and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility information are unchanged. v2 corrects one term and adds two attack-related citations without explaining their connection to the existing sparse-fusion argument. These limited edits establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
